전도서-11-1.title: 전도서 11장 1절 역사문법적 주해
전도서-11-1.exegesis: 20. thought-- literally, "consciousness." rich-- the great. The language, as applied to earthly princes knowing the "thought," is figurative. But it literally holds good of the King of kings ( Psa 139:1-24 ), whose consciousness of every evil thought we should ever realize. bed-chamber-- the most secret place ( 2Ki 6:12 ). bird of the air, &c.-- proverbial (compare Ha 2:11 ; Lu 19:40 ); in a way as marvellous and rapid, as if birds or some winged messenger carried to the king information of the curse so uttered. In the East superhuman sagacity was attributed to birds (see on Job 28:21 ; hence the proverb).

전도서-11-2.title: 전도서 11장 2절 역사문법적 주해
전도서-11-2.exegesis: CHAPTER 11 Ec 11:1-10 . 1. Ec 11:2 shows that charity is here inculcated. bread-- bread corn. As in the Lord's prayer, all things needful for the body and soul. Solomon reverts to the sentiment ( Ec 9:10 ). waters-- image from the custom of sowing seed by casting it from boats into the overflowing waters of the Nile, or in any marshy ground. When the waters receded, the grain in the alluvial soil sprang up ( Is 32:20 ). "Waters" express multitudes, so Ec 11:2 ; Re 17:15 ; also the seemingly hopeless character of the recipients of the charity; but it shall prove at last to have been not thrown away ( Is 49:4 ).

전도서-11-3.title: 전도서 11장 3절 역사문법적 주해
전도서-11-3.exegesis: 2. portion-- of thy bread. seven-- the perfect number. eight-- even to more than seven; that is, "to many" (so "waters," Ec 11:1 ), nay, even to very many in need ( Job 5:19 ; Mi 5:5 ). evil-- The day may be near, when you will need the help of those whom you have bound to you by kindnesses ( Lu 16:9 ). The very argument which covetous men use against liberality (namely, that bad times may come), the wise man uses for it.

전도서-11-4.title: 전도서 11장 4절 역사문법적 주해
전도서-11-4.exegesis: 3. clouds-- answering to "evil" ( Ec 11:2 ), meaning, When the times of evil are fully ripe, evil must come; and speculations about it beforehand, so as to prevent one sowing seed of liberality, are vain ( Ec 11:4 ). tree-- Once the storm uproots it, it lies either northward or southward, according as it fell. So man's character is unchangeable, whether for hell or heaven, once that death overtakes him ( Re 22:11 , 14, 15 ). Now is his time for liberality, before the evil days come ( Ec 12:1 ).

전도서-11-5.title: 전도서 11장 5절 역사문법적 주해
전도서-11-5.exegesis: 4. Therefore sow thy charity in faith, without hesitancy or speculation as to results, because they may not seem promising ( Ec 9:10 ). So in Ec 11:1 , man is told to "cast his bread corn" on the seemingly unpromising "waters" ( Psa 126:5 , 6 ). The farmer would get on badly, who, instead of sowing and reaping, spent his time in watching the wind and clouds.

전도서-11-6.title: 전도서 11장 6절 역사문법적 주해
전도서-11-6.exegesis: 5. spirit-- How the soul animates the body! Thus the transition to the formation of the body "in the womb" is more natural, than if with Maurer we translate it "wind" ( Ec 1:6 ; Joh 3:8 ). bones ... grow-- ( Job 10:8 , 9 ; Psa 139:15 , 16 ). knowest not the works of God-- ( Ec 3:11 ; 8:17 ; 9:12 ).

전도서-11-7.title: 전도서 11장 7절 역사문법적 주해
전도서-11-7.exegesis: 6. morning ... evening-- early and late; when young and when old; in sunshine and under clouds. seed-- of godly works ( Ho 10:12 ; 2Co 9:10 ; Ga 6:7 ). prosper-- ( Is 55:10 , 11 ). both ... alike-- Both the unpromising and the promising sowing may bear good fruit in others; certainly they shall to the faithful sower.

전도서-11-8.title: 전도서 11장 8절 역사문법적 주해
전도서-11-8.exegesis: 7. light-- of life ( Ec 7:11 ; Psa 49:19 ). Life is enjoyable, especially to the godly.
전도서-11-8.theologicalNote: 7. light-- of life ( Ec 7:11 ; Psa 49:19 ). Life is enjoyable, especially to the godly.

전도서-11-9.title: 전도서 11장 9절 역사문법적 주해
전도서-11-9.exegesis: 8. But while man thankfully enjoys life, "let him remember" it will not last for ever. The "many days of darkness," that is, the unseen world ( Job 10:21 , 22 ; Psa 88:12 ), also days of "evil" in this world ( Ec 11:2 ), are coming; therefore sow the good seed while life and good days last, which are not too long for accomplishing life's duties. All that cometh-- that is, All that followeth in the evil and dark days is vain, as far as work for God is concerned ( Ec 9:10 ).

전도서-11-10.title: 전도서 11장 10절 역사문법적 주해
전도서-11-10.exegesis: 9. Rejoice-- not advice, but warning. So 1Ki 22:15 , is irony; if thou dost rejoice (carnally, Ec 2:2 ; 7:2 , not moderately, as in Ec 5:18 ), &c., then "know that ... God will bring thee into judgment" ( Ec 3:17 ; 12:14 ). youth ... youth-- distinct Hebrew words, adolescence or boyhood (before Ec 11:10 ), and full-grown youth. It marks the gradual progress in self-indulgence, to which the young especially are prone; they see the roses, but do not discover the thorns, until pierced by them. Religion will cost self-denial, but the want of it infinitely more ( Lu 14:28 ).
